_about: Small list of laptop and PC chips and how well they work on OrionOS (Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 6.8 or newer). Read by os/windows/Check-OrionReady.ps1. Rules are tried in order and the first match wins, so specific chips come before 'any chip from this maker'. bus: PCI, USB, HDA (sound codec) or ACPI. vendor/device: the 4-digit hex ids Windows shows (VEN_xxxx&DEV_xxxx, VID_xxxx&PID_xxxx); acpi: the start of an ACPI id. status: good = works as soon as OrionOS starts; firmware = works, but needs extra firmware or a driver OrionOS installs, or a newer kernel; problem = often doesn't work on Linux yet. flavour (GPUs only): which OrionOS image to use.

rules.note: Intel Wi-Fi works out of the box (iwlwifi).
Realtek RTL8922AE (Wi-Fi 7) needs a newer kernel than some OrionOS builds have. Keep a USB Wi-Fi stick or a cable handy.
Realtek Wi-Fi works out of the box (rtw88 / rtw89).
Realtek Wi-Fi: most chips work; this one isn't in Orion's list. Have a cable or USB Wi-Fi stick ready for the first start.
MediaTek MT7902 has no reliable Linux driver yet. Use a USB Wi-Fi stick or a cable.
MediaTek MT7925 (Wi-Fi 7) works with Linux 6.8+ and current firmware; it can be unstable on early kernels.
MediaTek MT7921 / MT7922 works out of the box (mt7921e).
MediaTek Wi-Fi: most chips work; this one isn't in Orion's list.
Broadcom Wi-Fi needs Broadcom's own driver (bcmwl). Connect with a cable the first time so OrionOS can install it.
Broadcom Wi-Fi often needs an extra driver. Have a cable or USB Wi-Fi stick ready.
Qualcomm Atheros Wi-Fi works out of the box (ath9k / ath10k).
Qualcomm WCN6855 works (ath11k) but sleep and resume can be flaky on some laptops.
Qualcomm WCN7850 (Wi-Fi 7) needs current firmware (ath12k).
Qualcomm Wi-Fi: usually works with current firmware.
USB Wi-Fi: many work out of the box, some need a driver.
This Wi-Fi chip isn't in Orion's list. Try OrionOS from the USB stick first to see if it connects.
NVIDIA graphics: use the nvidia OrionOS image (it has NVIDIA's driver). With Secure Boot on, the first start asks you to enrol a key once.
AMD graphics work out of the box (amdgpu).
Intel graphics work out of the box.
Virtual machine graphics (Hyper-V).
Virtual machine graphics (VirtualBox).
Virtual machine graphics (VMware).
This graphics chip isn't in Orion's list. The standard image should still show a picture.
Intel Bluetooth works out of the box.
Realtek Bluetooth works out of the box.
MediaTek Bluetooth works out of the box.
Bluetooth (IMC Networks, a Realtek or MediaTek chip) usually works out of the box.
Bluetooth (Foxconn, a MediaTek or Qualcomm chip) usually works out of the box.
Broadcom Bluetooth may need extra firmware.
Bluetooth usually works out of the box.
This laptop uses Cirrus Logic speaker amplifiers. Headphones work; the built-in speakers may stay quiet until a firmware update for this model reaches Linux.
This laptop uses TI speaker amplifiers. The built-in speakers may need a newer kernel.
Realtek sound works out of the box.
Conexant sound works out of the box.
Sound works out of the box.
Intel sound works out of the box (on very new laptops the microphone may need a newer kernel).
AMD sound works out of the box.
Sound usually works out of the box.
Touchpads work out of the box (gestures included).
Goodix fingerprint readers mostly don't work on Linux. Orion's approvals use your phone's fingerprint instead.
Laptop fingerprint readers often don't work on Linux. Orion's approvals use your phone's fingerprint instead.
Wired network works out of the box.
